h: Making the Most of a Trafford Brick Day
p: The big plus here is everything around it. The Trafford Centre is one of the region's major shopping and leisure destinations, so food courts, restaurants and toilets are never far away, and there's plenty of parking for anyone coming by car. If you'd rather leave the car at home, the Metrolink tram line out to the Trafford Centre makes it a straightforward trip from the city centre.

SEA LIFE Manchester is also based at the Trafford Centre, so if the kids are on a roll you can pair bricks with sharks without moving the car. For older siblings who might be past the LEGO stage, Chill Factore's indoor real-snow slope is nearby at Trafford Quays, which is handy for keeping everyone happy on the same outing.

Inside, the best way to enjoy it is not to rush. Let the kids linger at the build tables, because that's often what they remember most, rather than ticking off every zone. Grown-ups should be ready to get stuck in too: a parent-and-child race car showdown is half the fun. Dress for crawling and climbing, bring a drink for the inevitable thirsty moment, and if you can manage a weekday outside the school holidays, you'll have far more elbow room at the brick pits.
Little tip for the drive home: a small tub of bricks in the car keeps the building buzz going.
